summary.headline: Aurum PropTech Q2 FY27 revenue rose 64% YoY to INR 130.2 crores, with EBITDA margin at 29.8% and a return to profit from continuing operations.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 was the fourth consecutive profitable quarter, with revenue from operations of INR 130.2 crores (up 64% YoY and 16% QoQ) and profit before tax from continuing operations of INR 6.8 crores. The Housing.com acquisition through Locon Solutions completed on September 29, 2026, in an all-stock deal, so its P&L is not in this quarter and will first appear in Q3. Balance sheet total assets rose to INR 1,641 crores and the group remains effectively debt-free, with lease liabilities of INR 216 crores. Management targets Housing.com profitability within 12 to 18 months, citing about INR 120 crores of cost cuts already executed.

segments.name: Distribution
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 69.7 crores (54% of group, +25% QoQ, 2.6x YoY); segment result INR 11.4 crores, a 16.3% margin, vs INR 8 crores in Q1. Q2 platform sold 117,000 leads (+79% YoY), 10,560 active technology licenses and facilitated INR 838 crores of home sales (gross commissions +144% YoY).

segments.name: Rental
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 56.1 crores (+10% YoY, +3% QoQ); segment profit INR 0.9 crores vs loss of INR 4.3 crores a year ago. Co-living and student living operated 16,500 beds at 82% occupancy across 137 buildings; residential rentals managed 8,900 signed units with INR 35 crores quarterly rent collected.

segments.name: Capital
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 4.3 crores (vs INR 1.6 crores in Q1 and INR 1.2 crores a year ago); segment broke even with INR 0.4 crores profit. KuberX disbursed INR 200 crores of loans in September 2026, run rate INR 2,400 crores.

guidance_outlook: Housing.com targeted to reach profitability within 12 to 18 months (management repeated this).
Breakeven for Housing.com: internal target 4 to 6 quarters, external target 6 to 8 quarters.
Expected Housing.com revenue growth of INR 100 to 150 crores over the next 4 to 6 quarters, which management says moves it to profitability; cost optimisation described as already done.
Revenue per team member expected to rise QoQ for the next 10 to 12 quarters; target of INR 56 lakhs by year-end vs INR 50-plus lakhs currently.
Rental occupancy projected at 88% by end of the year from 82%; management plans to grow beds across HelloWorld and NestAway.
Home loan disbursal target of INR 25,000 crores, reached in 4 to 6 quarters from the INR 2,400 crore run rate; synergies expected to show in the next two quarters.
Distribution segment to include a full quarter of Housing.com from Q3 FY27.
capex_capacity: Capex in H1 was INR 8.8 crores, mostly capitalised product development; lease principal payments were INR 47.8 crores in H1.
Co-living and student living: 16,500 beds, 82% occupancy, 137 buildings, with more than 90% occupancy in a subset of buildings.
Navi Mumbai building sale closed in Q1 for INR 112 crores, with a pre-tax gain of INR 52.4 crores (one-time, discontinued operations).
Purchase price allocation for Housing.com is provisional under Ind AS 103 and may be refined within the 12-month measurement period.
Lease liabilities of INR 216 crores, matched by INR 196.8 crores of right-of-use assets; goodwill and intangibles total INR 960 crores.
demand_pricing: Housing.com brings 58 million-plus monthly visits, 12 million monthly active users (1.2x nearest competitor), and a 52% share of app downloads among three measured platforms.
Channel partners: about 18,000–19,000 today, with a target of 50,000; developers: around 1,300-plus today, with a target of 4,000-plus across about 35 geographies.
Analytica works on 280 projects with 134 developers and sold 1.7 lakh leads in the quarter; Sell.do has 10,500-plus active licences.
Home loan take rate of 1% to 1.2% of disbursed value, earned as commission from banks.
Management says the platform benefits from both excess demand and excess supply in a two-sided marketplace, and expects developer marketing spend to rise in a slowdown.
Competitive context: management cited a listed peer reporting EBITDA-positive marketplace results; leadership now concentrated among 2 or 3 platforms.

qa_highlights.question: How would the business be affected if real estate prices fell 15 to 20% in a hypothetical downturn?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it would cut the cost base and temporarily pause activity in affected micro-markets. It argued that slowdowns tend to raise developer sales and marketing spend, which benefits platforms; it gave no quantified sensitivity.

qa_highlights.question: Can KuberX scale to match Square Yards' mortgage-led revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: KuberX disbursed INR 200 crores in September (INR 2,400 crore run rate). Management targets INR 25,000 crores of disbursement within 4 to 6 quarters; it is currently run within the PropTiger team.

qa_highlights.question: What is Housing.com's expected profit contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is too early to give projections, as the deal closed on September 30. It cited a path to profitability and a strong integration plan.

qa_highlights.question: What is the breakeven timeline, and what if the real estate cycle softens?
qa_highlights.answer: Internal breakeven target is 4 to 6 quarters and external target 6 to 8 quarters, with profitability expected before that. Management said a price softening could be turned into an opportunity.

qa_highlights.question: What are the integration cost cuts and revenue synergies for Housing.com, and what is the AI spend?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 120 crores of costs were cut within the first week. Future growth is expected to come from INR 100 to 150 crores of revenue over 4 to 6 quarters. AI investment is focused on the consumer journey, with no tangible results yet.

qa_highlights.question: What are the tax losses acquired with Housing.com, and will the group pay less tax?
qa_highlights.answer: Housing.com brings about INR 1,020 crores of carry-forward losses. Management said tax planning is at an early stage and that it is taking further advice on how to use them.

risks_watch: Housing.com is still loss-making: profitability is targeted in 12 to 18 months and breakeven in 4 to 8 quarters, dependent on INR 100 to 150 crores of revenue growth.
Purchase price allocation is provisional, with goodwill and intangibles of INR 960 crores (about 58% of total assets), so future impairment risk is material.
Rental bed and unit counts fell QoQ; management attributed this to NestAway consolidation and a one-time HelloWorld reduction in Q1 FY27. Watch for bed growth resuming.
Effective tax rate of about 37% because losses in some subsidiaries are not recognised as tax assets; the INR 1,020 crore Housing carry-forward loss use is unclear.
Distribution's other-expense ratio rose to 47.8% from 45% in Q1 as higher-variable-cost distribution grew fastest.
Management said it is not pursuing acquisitions in the short run, with bandwidth focused on integration.
Deferred tax liability of INR 50.4 crores and INR 88.5 crores of remaining warrant payments (due within 18 months of the 51 lakh warrants issued to the promoter).
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on growth, AI and the Housing.com thesis, with specific targets (breakeven timelines, INR 25,000 crore loan goal). Answers on Housing.com's standalone profitability, tax losses and the downside scenario were hedged as "early days" or "too early" and lacked quantification.
key_quotes: We are targeting to make Housing.com profitable within 12 to 18 months; I repeat, within 12 to 18 months.

The cost optimization is already done. We believe that there will be revenue growth of another INR100 crores, INR150 crores over next four to six quarters, which will kind of move Housing.com to profitability.
So we believe that we will not do something inorganic in our short run for sure.
It's still early days, Jayesh to kind of talk about the quarter or the annual numbers on housing.

adds.what: Housing.com platform acquisition via Locon Solutions (all-stock, completed Sep 29, 2026); not an organic capacity addition but adds revenue base from Q3

growth.why: Management guides Housing.com to add INR 100-150 crore revenue over 4-6 quarters and to reach profitability in 12-18 months, backed by a 82% occupied bed base, 16,500 beds targeted to rise to 88% occupancy, a home loan run-rate targeted to rise from INR 2,400 crore to INR 25,000 crore, and cost cuts of about INR 120 crore already done; the revenue ramp is supported by the acquisition and demand me
